subject: Post-call: Telemetry & evals — scope, acceptance criteria and next steps
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Ortiz <elena.ortiz@fintechco.com>, Kyle Ramos <kyle@finpilot.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 16 Jul 2026 13:05:00 -0400
Subject: Post-call: Telemetry & evals — scope, acceptance criteria and next steps

Hi Elena / Kyle — thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our call and proposed next steps so we have alignment.

Pain points you called out:
- No token-level cost visibility across prompts; engineering only sees aggregated spend in infra metrics.
- Recent model updates caused regressions in a few user journeys (invoice parsing + customer support routing).
- Lack of standardized golden prompt sets and reproducible evals for releases.
- Minimal tracing hooks into the LLM stack (hard to correlate request -> model variant -> latency/cost).

Current stack (as I captured it):
- Frontend -> internal API -> calls OpenAI hosted endpoints (mixed models).
- Logging/metrics: Datadog for infra; in-house event store for business events (no token-level breakdown).
- CI/CD: model updates managed as code, but no automated quality gate for LLM behavior.

Success criteria you mentioned:
1) Token-level cost dashboard by route (sufficient to attribute to product features)
2) Regression alerting for golden prompts with <5% false positive rate
3) Tracing hook that surfaces model variant and latency per request in your existing traces
4) A rollout guardrail policy so you can safely canary new model versions for 2 weeks

Deliverables we propose for PoC (2–4 weeks):
- Sample telemetry dashboard (token cost by route + anomaly charts) — attachment: redwood-eval-playbook.pdf (slide with dashboard template).
- Tracing snippet + integration notes for your event store and Datadog.
- Golden prompts template + regression test harness (we'll provide runner + example prompts).
- Suggested rollout guardrail config (canary %s, rollback thresholds, automatic fallback).

Immediate next steps:
1) I will send the dashboard template + playbook (attached).
2) Elena / Kyle to share a small export of 1 week of recent requests (anonymized) and a short list of 6–8 golden prompts you care about (format: JSONL). You can drop it in the Drive link we shared or reply with the file.
3) Internal: Marissa & Dev, can you prepare the tracing snippet + short implementation doc and estimate effort (hours) for FintechCo integration?

Timeline: we think a focused PoC (dashboard + tracing + 6 golden prompts regression run) is achievable in ~3 weeks with a single dedicated engineer from each side.

Thanks — happy to jump on a follow-up if you want to walk the deliverables.

Best,
Dylan Brooks
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
D: +1 (415) 555-0129
redwood.ai

Attachment: redwood-eval-playbook.pdf (12 pages) — dashboard templates, regression harness notes
Attachment: fintechco-current-stack.csv (export of endpoints and routes you shared during call)

From: Elena Ortiz <elena.ortiz@fintechco.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 16 Jul 2026 15:12:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: Telemetry & evals — scope, acceptance criteria and next steps

Dylan — thanks for the clear recap. Confirming a few small clarifications so the PoC hits our internal acceptance criteria:

1) Token-level cost dashboard: must be able to slice by product route (invoicing, support-bot, reconciliation) and by model family (Llama2-70B, Llama2-13B, etc.). Ideally the dashboard ties back to our billing tags.
2) Regression alerts: we want a daily summary + immediate alert if any golden prompt fails more than 10% against the baseline during canary. We can tune false positives after the first week.
3) Tracing hooks: we can add a span in our API gateway that includes model_variant and token_count; our SRE will accept a small instrumentation snippet.

I'll upload a 7-day anonymized request export and 8 candidate golden prompts by EOD tomorrow to the Drive link. Also attaching a short sheet that lists our product routes (will send as separate file).

One other ask: can you include an estimated monthly unit cost delta for token-level caching and prefix caching suggestions? We need a rough TCO delta to present to our finance partner.

Happy to chat further.

— Elena
Head of Platform, FintechCo
elena.ortiz@fintechco.com

Attachment: fintechco-product-routes.xlsx (stub)

Subject: Re: Post-call: Telemetry & evals — scope, acceptance criteria and next steps

Internal owners — looped you in to start the engineering estimate and cost delta for caching. Key asks from Elena:
- Dashboard slices by route + model family (dashboard tile + SQL/metric queries)
- Regression alerting: daily summary + immediate alert on >10% failures during canary
- Tracing snippet (small span) for gateway that includes model_variant and token_count
- TCO delta: monthly estimate for prefix caching + token-level caching recommendations (two scenarios: conservative vs aggressive)

Marissa — can you own the dashboard template + regression harness delivery? Suggest we reuse the dashboard example in the attached playbook but add FintechCo route names.
Dev — can you draft the tracing snippet and estimate hours for integration with their gateway and Datadog?
Mateo — can you build a rough cost model for caching (assume their weekly request export will be ~200k tokens/day) and produce both conservative/aggressive numbers for Elena. Put numbers in a shareable slide.

I'll draft an intro email for procurement once we've got the PoC scope. Aim to have rough estimates and the first slide pack by EOD tomorrow.

Thanks — Dylan
